exposure: conservative treatment for endometrial intraepithelial neoplasm (EIN)
conservative treatment for early endometrial cancer (EC)
outcome: radical surgery due to condition deterioration
cohort: 87 women who were conservatively treated for atypical hyperplasia, endometrial intraepithelial neoplasm, and well-differentiated endometrioid endometrial cancer confined to the endometrium over a 10-year period.
finding: This study demonstrated the efficacy and safety of current conservative treatment protocols for AH/EIN/EC, highlighting that an adequate early (6-month) response to therapy is crucial for achieving long-term remission and successful pregnancy.
mod_finding: Among the successful pregnancies, seven resulted in a term delivery of a healthy child, mostly through planned cesarean section.
followup_time: up to 10 years (data collection period); long-term for oncologic outcomes (beyond 12 months post-therapy)
gest_age: N/A (though 'term delivery' is an outcome, no specific range for the cohort's babies is provided)
